generated_by: Hand-written expectations (G-326), written before any language ran; args_digest computed from the RFC 8785 rule by the generator, not by a harness. Each language's runner drives its real runtime with a fake model client and asserts the outcome equals `expected`; `result` records those measured outcomes.
pins_note: Which approval-gated calls a host ToolPolicy lets run without asking, and which policies are refused before any run. The fake model asks for `calls` in its first step, then answers. Every tool needs approval by mode. A tool with `server` is provided at resolve time (an MCP server); one without is a native, statically registered tool. Recorded: `refused` (the error code when the policy is refused at construction or at install), the tools that ran, the tools of the last response's pending approvals, and the decision events projected to type, server, tool, args_digest, decided_by and policy_revision. `then` replaces the policy and resumes with no decision.

cases.title: a listed native tool runs without asking
cases.notes: Baseline: the one thing the list is for.

cases.title: a trailing space on the called name never matches
cases.notes: The tool is registered padded; the list names it clean.

cases.title: a trailing no-break space never matches
cases.notes: U+00A0, which PHP trim() leaves and JS trim() strips.

cases.title: a trailing zero-width space never matches
cases.notes: U+200B: invisible, and stripped by no language's trim().

cases.title: a leading BOM never matches
cases.notes: U+FEFF, which Python strip() leaves.

cases.title: a Cyrillic homoglyph never matches
cases.notes: U+0435 for the e.

cases.title: a fullwidth look-alike never matches
cases.notes: U+FF52 U+FF45 U+FF41 U+FF44, which NFKC would fold to read.

cases.title: a case variant never matches
cases.notes: No case folding.

cases.title: an unscoped entry never matches an MCP tool of the same name
cases.notes: The MCP shadow: a server offers `search` and the host listed only a native `search`.

cases.title: an entry for another server never matches
cases.notes: Scoped to files; the tool comes from web.

cases.title: an entry scoped to the tool's own server matches
cases.notes: The way to allow an MCP tool.

cases.title: a scoped entry never matches the native tool of the same name
cases.notes: The reverse shadow.

cases.title: a listed tool that declares destructive is refused at construction
cases.notes: The host learns of it; nothing is silently dropped.

cases.title: a destructive MCP tool asks even when listed
cases.notes: Its provider is only known per session, so construction cannot see the tier; the call still asks.

cases.title: honor false turns the list off
cases.notes: For example, an untrusted workspace.

cases.title: a padded entry is refused at construction
cases.notes: Rather than normalised into a match.

cases.title: a homoglyph entry is refused at construction
cases.notes: ASCII-only names.

cases.title: a wildcard entry is refused at construction
cases.notes: No wildcards, patterns or prefixes.

cases.title: a confirmation tool is refused at construction
cases.notes: Only a person may run it.

cases.title: an approval tool behind a dot is refused at construction
cases.notes: Every separator splits a token.

cases.title: a camelCase confirmation tool is refused at construction
cases.notes: A camelCase boundary splits a token.

cases.title: a padded confirmation tool is refused at construction
cases.notes: G-36: the reservation normalises first.

cases.title: a name merely containing a reserved verb is not reserved
cases.notes: Whole tokens only: send_confirmation_email stays listable.

cases.title: an unknown entry key is refused at construction
cases.notes: A constraint this version does not enforce must not be silently ignored.

cases.title: a listed and an unlisted call in one step
cases.notes: The unlisted one asks; the listed one runs. Asked is recorded before the listed call runs.

cases.title: the digest is of RFC 8785 canonical arguments
cases.notes: Keys in UTF-16 order, ECMAScript numbers. Never the arguments themselves.

cases.title: a pending call stays pending when a later policy would allow it
cases.notes: Nothing listed; the call asks. The host then lists it and resumes with no decision: it is refused, not run.
